title: Existence of normalized core comparison between system operations
statement: Fix a prime l and a finite extension E of Q_l in the coefficient universe, and let o,d be any two normalized TensorOperations packages on the strict quotient sequence categories [def-pur-system-tensor-mate-arrows]. There exists a core comparison [def-pur-system-tensor-presentation-core] between o and d: pullback, open extension, and tensor comparisons with identity K-flat normalization, both proper and open adjunction unit/counit equations, canonical pullback compositor compatibility, and mu compatibility. This statement contains no semilinear source realization, no coefficient universe lift, and no projection or open tensor mate equation.

proof.text: Construct the ordinary comparison $c_W$ by $(c_WM)(a,U)=M_{a+1}(U)$, with horizontal restriction the given semilinear transition and vertical restriction the sheaf restriction. The vertical covering condition is exactly the sheaf condition for each $M_{a+1}$; compatibility of the two restrictions is exactly that a transition is a morphism of module sheaves. Restriction to the vertical slices recovers $M$ and its transitions. These two constructions are inverse also on morphisms. This is an additive equivalence, and is exact because exactness in both presentations is componentwise. Apply it termwise to complexes. It and its inverse preserve quasi-isomorphisms; the localization universal property descends the two functors and their inverse identities. This constructs the asserted $C_W$, on the whole unbounded derived category.

proof.text: The ordinary tensor comparison for $c_W$ is fixed by $x\otimes y\mapsto x\otimes y$ at $(a,U)$, with both sides balanced over $(A_{a+1})_W(U)$. Indeed both tensors are the sheafification of these sectionwise balanced tensor products; a vertical matching family and its gluing are unchanged by $c_W$. The inverse uses the same formula. Horizontal compatibility is the equality $\rho(x\otimes y)=\rho(x)\otimes\rho(y)$ with the actual quotient-semilinear restrictions. The coefficient-unit comparison is the identity. On local pure tensors the associator, unitors and symmetry are the same reassociation, scalar multiplication and interchange maps, respectively; hence their coherence diagrams commute. Thus $c_W$ and its inverse are an exact symmetric strong monoidal equivalence. This is an ordinary sheaf construction, without any assertion that derived evaluation detects equality.

proof.text: Apply the exact monoidal equivalence total-tensor theorem to $c_W$. Its hypotheses hold: these are Grothendieck module categories, and the sheaf tensor is additive and preserves coproducts in each variable. The canonical coproduct comparison and the preceding tensorator give the comparison on every signed $(p,q)$ total summand. The theorem preserves flat terms and K-flat complexes in both directions. Consequently the published K-flat representative models give $C_W(M\otimes^LN)\cong C_WM\otimes^LC_WN$. The cochain tensor-model rigidity theorem makes this a unique natural comparison with the given total-summand formula, independent of resolutions. Its full-faithfulness assertion extends the coherence equalities from representatives to arbitrary derived objects. This proves the tensor comparison before evaluation, including for complexes unbounded in both directions.

proof.text: On ordinary systems, $c_Yu_*$ and $u_*^{\rm diag}c_X$ have the same sections: both evaluate $M_{a+1}$ on the base-changed site object and restrict scalars by the constant-section structural ring map. The maps on sections and the horizontal transitions are unchanged; the structural ring maps agree by the constant-scalar uniqueness in the specified diagram presentation. Conjugate the ordinary system pullback adjunction by $c_X,c_Y$. It and the specified diagram pullback are left adjoints of this same direct image. The unit-equation uniqueness lemma gives the canonical pullback comparison carrying one unit to the other. Their counits then agree: the transpose of each counit is the identity under the identified Hom bijections. For an open, restriction is already identified by the same construction; applying the lemma to its two left adjoints gives $c_Yj_!\cong j_!^{\rm diag}c_X$ and identifies the open unit and counit.

proof.text: The exact pullbacks and open extensions descend termwise with their ordinary comparisons. For direct image choose a system K-injective resolution $H\to I$. An exact equivalence preserves K-injectivity and resolutions, by the exact-postcomposition K-injective descent theorem. Both total right derived functors have units that are isomorphisms on K-injective complexes, with $R_uH\cong Q(u_*I)$ and $R_u^{\rm diag}C_XH\cong Q(u_*^{\rm diag}c_XI)$ [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]. Thus the section comparison of Step 4 gives $C_YR_uH\cong R_u^{\rm diag}C_XH$, computed by the ordinary comparison on $I$. The universal property of these derived units makes this independent of $I$ and natural for all derived morphisms. The derived adjunctions in the two presentations are the canonical derived adjunctions of these ordinary ones. On complexes with K-injective target their Hom bijections are localization of the ordinary transpose, so Step 4 identifies those bijections. Their unit is the transpose of an identity and their counit the inverse transpose of an identity; hence the comparisons identify the specified derived units and counits. This gives all three operation comparisons, without assuming that evaluation preserves K-injectives.

proof.text: For composable maps, the ordinary direct-image compositor is section restriction along the same fibre-product pasting map in either presentation. Reindexing changes neither that map nor any section. Its derived compositor is computed on a K-injective $I$ through the derived units [def-sfb-right-derived-functor]; the intermediate direct image is K-injective because its left adjoint is exact. The composition clause of K-injective descent therefore identifies these specified derived compositors. Pullback compositors are the adjunction conjugates of the direct-image ones. Substitution in the mate formula, using the unit and counit equalities from Steps 4-5, identifies their pullback conjugates as well. In particular this applies to open restrictions and to the two paths around a commutative square. Identity compositors agree by the same section and mate formulas.

proof.text: Check the pullback tensor comparison with its specified normalization. Use the geometric structures supplied by semilinear-operations existence; unpacking Geometry gives precisely the ordinary pure-tensor comparison and the total-representative normalization of the geometric-derived interface. Under Step 4 the two ordinary direct-image lax tensor maps agree, because both send a local pure tensor to that same tensor on the pulled-back object. The unit equations of Step 4 then identify their adjunction transposes, hence the ordinary inverse-image tensor comparisons. On flat-term K-flat system complexes the two derived comparisons, after Step 3, consequently have the same inverse ordinary comparison followed by the actual $(p,q)$ summand inclusion. This equality includes the signed total differential. The representative localization equations identify the localized maps. Apply cochain tensor-model full faithfulness on the source ringed system category, with target the diagram category on $X$, to extend this equality to all pairs of derived inputs. This proves identification of $\mu_u$ itself, rather than only of its evaluation.
